harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a local root CA named "OS Comparison Root CA" on node1 (RHEL 10) and installed it as a trusted system CA via update-ca-trust. Verified functionally by issuing a leaf certificate and confirming it validates against the system default trust store, both before and after a full node restart (boot ID changed, confirming a genuine reboot).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 10.0) and found openssl missing; installed it via dnf
Generated CA private key and self-signed root certificate (CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison, 4096-bit RSA, SHA256, 10yr validity) under /etc/pki/ca-os-comparison/
Copied the CA certificate to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and ran update-ca-trust extract to install it as a trusted system CA
Verified the CA appears in `trust list` as an anchor and in the system ca-bundle.crt
Issued a leaf certificate signed by the new CA and confirmed `openssl verify` (using only the system default trust store) returned OK, proving functional trust
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline, restarted node1 via `shutdown -r now`, polled until the node was reachable again, and confirmed the boot_id changed (proving a real reboot)

Post-reboot, re-verified the CA anchor, ca-bundle entry, and anchor file persisted, and re-ran the leaf-certificate issue+verify test to prove the trust configuration survived and is functionally working after restart

evidence.requirement: CA created with correct name (OS Comparison Root CA) on node1
evidence.summary: Generated rootCA.key and rootCA.crt; openssl x509 -subject confirms CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison, self-signed (issuer==subject)

evidence.requirement: CA certificate installed as trusted system CA
evidence.summary: Copied cert to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and ran update-ca-trust extract; `trust list` shows it as a trust:anchor entry and it appears once in /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt

evidence.requirement: Functional proof the CA is trusted system-wide (not just present in a list)
evidence.summary: Issued a leaf certificate signed by the new CA and ran `openssl verify` with no explicit CA file (system default trust store) — result: leaf.crt: OK
Captured boot_id=19062a82-6390-435d-a09f-4dba1593d529 and confirmed CA anchor/trust status prior to restart
Issued `shutdown -r now` in background; exec stream closed as node went down, confirming the restart command was accepted and executed

evidence.requirement: Node restart availability and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Polled node1 (two timeouts while down, then success); boot_id changed to b03e9a91-4e57-4060-b92b-1c2d67e0f9f9, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of CA trust configuration and functional health
evidence.summary: After reboot, `trust list` still shows OS Comparison Root CA as anchor, ca-bundle.crt still contains it, anchor file intact, and a freshly issued leaf cert verified OK against the system trust store
